chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who confessed to an heir a debt during his illness, so he said: 'A bequest to an heir is not valid, nor is a confession.' The way to understand this report is to assume it is based on a type of precautionary concealment (taqiyyah), because it is the view of all those who differed from the Shia in refusing to validate the bequest to the heir, and this is its ruling: taqiyyah is valid in it.

key_terms.مَرَض: Illness (specifically the period of death illness)

ai.seo_question: Is a dying person's confession of debt to an heir legally valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a dying person's confession of debt to an heir is legally invalid, mirroring the prohibition of bequests to heirs. The scholar attributes this ruling to *taqiyyah* (precautionary concealment), noting that it aligns with the consensus of other Sunni schools who also rejected such bequests, thereby preventing sectarian dispute. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of using *taqiyyah* to maintain unity and avoid unnecessary conflict with the broader Muslim community.
